record.title: China extends suspension of six export-control measures covering rare earths, batteries and graphite
record.summary: China’s Ministry of Commerce and General Administration of Customs announced on Nov 9, 2026 that the suspension of six 2025 export-control announcements will continue from Nov 11, 2026 through Jan 10, 2027. The Ministry’s official 2025 announcement index identifies those measures as controls on superhard materials; rare-earth equipment and inputs; medium and heavy rare earths; lithium batteries and artificial-graphite anode materials; certain foreign-produced rare-earth items; and rare-earth technology. The notice documents a time-limited change in the status of these measures. It does not show resulting shipment volumes, licensing outcomes, prices, or effects on AI hardware and compute supply.
organizations: Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China
General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On Nov 9, 2026, China’s Ministry of Commerce and General Administration of Customs issued Announcement 2026 No. 58, stating that the suspension of six 2025 export-control announcements continues from Nov 11, 2026 through Jan 10, 2027.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Ministry’s official 2025 announcement index identifies the covered announcements as controls concerning superhard materials, rare-earth equipment and inputs, medium and heavy rare earths, lithium batteries and artificial-graphite anode materials, certain foreign-produced rare-earth items, and rare-earth technology.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected official notices do not establish realized shipment or licensing changes, price effects, or a direct impact on AI hardware, semiconductor production, or compute availability.

evidence_gaps.description: No export volumes, license approvals, prices, inventory changes or supplier responses were inspected for the six categories.
The current sources do not identify a direct link between the covered categories and an observed AI hardware, semiconductor or compute supply constraint.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as announced, the extension changes near-term trade-control conditions across several technology-relevant material and equipment categories. That is notable for hardware supply chains, but no measured AI-compute consequence is reported.
limitations: The notice states the suspension period but does not provide implementation data or explain whether any other licensing requirements apply outside these six measures.
The measure is relevant to broad technology-material supply chains; direct AI-sector effects are not established.
The review inspected the official notice and the Ministry’s announcement index, not underlying shipment records or all six original notices.
organizations: Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China

technical.claimed_result: No separate technical-performance result is claimed. The potential relevance is to technology-material supply conditions, not a measured AI capability or compute effect.
technical.compute_or_cost: No compute-price, AI-infrastructure cost or shipment data reported in the inspected notice.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Nov 9 notice states that the suspension of the six named measures continues from Nov 11, 2026 through Jan 10, 2027.
technical.implementation_status: Officially announced; trade flows and case-level licensing outcomes were not inspected.
technical.mechanism: A time-limited suspension changes whether six specified 2025 export-control notices are implemented during the stated period. The release does not describe the operational licensing path or other controls.
technical.regime: China’s six specified 2025 export-control notices concerning superhard materials, rare-earth items and technology, lithium batteries and artificial-graphite anode materials; announced suspension period Nov 11, 2026–Jan 10, 2027.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to a policy notice; implementation outcomes require later trade and licensing data.
technical.strongest_baseline: The preceding official suspension, Announcement 2025 No. 70, ran through Nov 10, 2026; the Nov 9, 2026 No. 58 notice extends the suspension from Nov 11 through Jan 10, 2027.

brief.title: China extends suspension of six export-control measures covering rare earths, batteries and graphite
brief.why_it_matters: Export-control conditions for rare-earth inputs, battery materials, graphite anodes and related equipment can affect technology manufacturing supply chains. The official notice documents a two-month continuation of suspension for six specified measures; it does not establish that AI hardware or compute supply changed.
